frequency_question: How often does a central bank implement an incremental cash reserve ratio tool when faced with surplus liquidity conditions within a comparable time frame?
membership_rule: Includes any formal deployment of temporary, marginal, or incremental reserve ratios by major central banks (such as the Reserve Bank of India, People's Bank of China, or Bank of England) designed to absorb specific liquidity overhangs over a defined execution window. Excludes standard, permanent changes to baseline reserve requirement ratios.

cases.name: PBOC reserve requirement ratio targeted/marginal adjustments
RBI secondary liquidity absorption framework adjustments
PBOC dynamic/incremental RRR deployment for credit control

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named primary instances of targeted incremental reserve requirements by central banks during excess liquidity phases; universe is small because incremental RRR is a specialized instrument.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or opaque administrative liquidity directives from smaller emerging market central banks due to reporting consistency.
skeleton: Central bank liquidity management cycles requiring targeted quantity tools over past decades, parsed by policy intervention frequency.
multiplier: 4 instances of targeted incremental reserve tool deployments across major systemic liquidity overhang cycles over 25 years.
validity_reason: Central bank operational toolkits and preference for targeted liquidity management instruments evolve slowly across decades.
